question.problem:
Determine whether $v=[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].$
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
question.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2+2\text{i} \\ 4-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2{\text{i}}^{2}+2\text{i} \\ 4-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\text{i}(2-2\text{i}) \\ 2(2-2\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =(2-2\text{i})[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =(2-2\text{i})v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Av=(2-2\text{i})v,$ we conclude that $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda =2-2\text{i}.$
